questions.q: Moment of inertia of a square plate of side $l$ about the axis passing through one of the corner and perpendicular to the plane of square plate is given by:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Use parallel axis theorem to get the magnitude of the moment of inertia& of a square plate of side& $l$~about the axis passing through one of the corners and perpendicular to the plane of a square plate,~

${I}_{z} = {I}_{cm} + M\left(\dfrac{l}{2}\right)2$

$⇒ {I}_{z} = \dfrac{Ml^{2}}{6} + \dfrac{Ml^{2}}{2} = \dfrac{4Ml^{2}}{6} = \dfrac{2Ml^{2}}{3}$.

questions.q: A force of 49 N acts tangentially at the highest point of a sphere (solid) of mass 20 kg , kept on a rough horizontal plane. If the sphere rolls without slipping, then the acceleration of the center of the sphere is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Torque about bottom point
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{F} \times 2 \mathrm{r}=\mathrm{I} \alpha \\ & 49 \times 2 \mathrm{r}=\frac{7}{5} \mathrm{mr}^2 \alpha \\ & 14=4 \mathrm{r} \alpha
\end{aligned}$
As sphere rolls without slipping
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{a}=\mathrm{r} \alpha \\ & \mathrm{a}=\frac{14}{4}=\frac{7}{2}=3.5 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: Moment of inertia of a body about a given axis is $1.5kgm^{2} .$ Initially the body is at rest. In order to produce a rotational kinetic energy of $1200J,$ the angular acceleration of $20rad / s^{2}$ must be applied about the axis for a duration of:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
We know that,&

Rotational kinetic energy,& $K = \dfrac{1}{2}I{ω}^{2}$~

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2}I{ω}^{2} = 1200$
$⇒ \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1 .5 \times {ω}^{2} = 1200$
$⇒ \omega = 40rads^{- 1}$

We also know that,~$\omega = \alphat$
$⇒ t = \dfrac{40}{20} = 2s$

questions.q: A thin circular disc of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is rotating in a horizontal plane about an axis passing through its centre and perpendicular to its plane with angular velocity $\omega$. If another disc of same dimensions but of mass $\mathrm{M} / 2$ is placed gently on the first disc co-axially, then the new angular velocity of the system is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{I}_1 \omega=\mathrm{I}_2 \omega_2 \\ & \frac{\mathrm{MR}^2}{2} \omega=\frac{3}{2}\left(\frac{\mathrm{MR}^2}{2}\right) \omega_2 \\ & \omega_2=\frac{2}{3} \omega\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A solid cylinder and a solid sphere, having same mass $M$ and radius $R$, roll down the same inclined plane from top without slipping. They start from rest. The ratio of velocity of the solid cylinder to that of the solid sphere, with which they reach the ground, will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
During pure rolling, the work done by the friction is zero. Therefore, we can apply conservation of mechanical energy.

$mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}I\left(\dfrac{v}{R}\right)2$

$⇒ mgh = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(m + \dfrac{I}{R2}\right)v^{2}$

$⇒ v = \sqrt{\dfrac{2gh}{1 + \dfrac{I}{mR^{2}}}}$

For a solid cylinder~$\dfrac{I}{mR^{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2}$~and for a solid sphere,~$\dfrac{I}{mR^{2}} = \dfrac{2}{5}$

$\dfrac{vCyl}{vSph} = \sqrt{\dfrac{1 + \dfrac{2}{5}}{1 + \dfrac{1}{2}}}= \sqrt{\dfrac{14}{15}}$

questions.subject: Physics

It can be assumed as several parts of discs having different radius, so

$I = ∫ dl = ∫ dm \left(r^{2}\right)$

From diagram

\dfrac{r}{y} ==$tan\text{\theta} = $\dfrac{R}{H}$

$r = \dfrac{R}{H} \cdoty$

$dm = $\text{ρ}\left(\text{\pi}$r^{2}\right)dy$

From equation (i), (ii) and (iii)

$I = \dfrac{MR^{2}}{2}$

$

questions.q: Two masses $m$ and $\dfrac{m}{2}$ are connected at the two ends of a massless rigid rod of length $l .$ The rod is suspended by a thin wire of torsional constant $k$ at the centre of mass of the rod-mass system (see figure). Because of torsional constant $k,$ the restoring torque is $τ = k\theta$ for angular displacement $\theta .$ If the rod is rotated by ${\theta}_{0}$ and released, the tension in it when it passes through its mean position will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When rod is rotated by angle $\alpha,$ the twist in the wire is $ϕ .$

angular frequency of wire, $Ω = \sqrt{\dfrac{k}{I}}$

angular frequency of rod, $\omega = {\theta}_{0} . Ω$

Max. Tension in the rod $= m{\omega}^{2} . \dfrac{l}{3}$

$= m{\theta}_{0}^{2} . \dfrac{k}{I} . \dfrac{l}{3},$ here $I = m\dfrac{l^{2}}{3}$

$= {\theta}_{0}^{2}\dfrac{k}{l}$

questions.q: A thin circular ring of mass $M$ and radius $R$ is rotating with a constant angular velocity $2rads^{- 1}$~in a horizontal plane about an axis vertical to its plane and passing through the center of the ring. If two objects each of mass $m$ be attached gently to the opposite ends of a diameter of ring, the ring will then rotate with an angular velocity (in~$rads^{- 1}$).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As the masses are gently placed we can apply conservation of angular momentum.

Initial moment of Inertia& ${I}_{1} = MR^{2}$

Final moment of inertia~${I}_{2} = MR^{2} + \left(2m\right)R^{2}$

By conservation of angular momentum

${I}_{1}{ω}_{1} = {I}_{2}{ω}_{2}⇒ MR^{2} \times 2 = \left(M + 2m\right)R^{2} \times {ω}_{2}$

$⇒ {ω}_{2} = \dfrac{2M}{M + 2m}rads^{- 1}$

questions.solution:
Only the translational kinetic energy of disc changes into gravitational potential energy and rotational $KE$ remains unchanged as there is no friction.

$\dfrac{1}{2}mv^{2} = mgh$

$⇒ h = \dfrac{v2}{2g}$

questions.q: The linear mass density of a thin rod& $AB$~of length~$L$~varies from~$A$~to~$B$~as~$\lambda \left(x\right) = {λ}_{0} \left($1 + $\dfrac{x}{L}\right), where~$x$~is the distance from~$A$. If~$M$~is the mass of the rod then its moment of inertia~about an axis passing through~$A$ \text{ and } and perpendicular to the rod :$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$dm = \lambda . dv$

$dI = dm . x^{2}$

$= {λ}_{0}\left(1 + \dfrac{x}{L}\right) . x^{2}dx$

$I = {λ}_{0}{∫}_{0}^{1}\left(x^{2} + \dfrac{x3}{L}\right)dx$

$= {λ}_{0}{\dfrac{x3}{3} + \dfrac{x4}{4L}}_{0}^{L}$

$= {λ}_{0} \left[\dfrac{L3}{3} + \dfrac{L3}{4}\right]

$I = $\dfrac{7{λ}_{0}L^{3}}{12}

$m = \mathop{∫}_{0}^{L}\lambda dx = $\dfrac{3{λ}_{0}L}{2}

\dfrac{I}{m} = \dfrac{7L^{2}}{12 \times \dfrac{3}{2}} = \dfrac{7L^{2}}{18}

$⇒$~$I = \dfrac{7}{18}{mL}^{2}$

$

questions.q:
A huge circular arc of length $4 . 4ly$ subtends an angle $4s$ at the centre of the circle. How long it would take for a body to complete $4$ revolution if its speed is $8AU$ per second?
Given : $1ly = 9 . 46 \times {10}^{15}m$

$1AU = 1 . 5 \times {10}^{11}m$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$ℓ = 4 . 4ly = 4 . 4 \times 9 . 46 \times {10}^{15}$

length of Arc. $= ℓ = R\theta$

$4 . 4 \times 9 . 46 \times {10}^{15} = R\theta$

$\theta = 4S = 4 \times 4 . 843 \times {10}^{- 6} = 1 . 94 \times {10}^{- 5}$~rad

$4 . 4 \times 9 . 46 \times {10}^{15} = R \times 1 . 94 \times {10}^{- 5}$

$R = 2 . 1455 \times {10}^{21}$ meter

Speed $= 8Au = 8 \times 1 . 5 \times {10}^{11}\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1} = 12 \times {10}^{11}\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$

$4$ revolution means distance $= 4 \times 2\piR$ metre

time~$= \dfrac{ distance }{ speed } = \dfrac{4 \times 2\piR}{12 \times {10}^{11}};$~time~$= \dfrac{8 \times 3 . 14 \times 2 . 1455 \times {10}^{21}}{12 \times {10}^{11}} ⇒ 4 . 5 \times {10}^{10}sec$

questions.q: The torque of a force $5\overset{^}{i} + 3\overset{^}{j} - 7\overset{^}{k}$ about the origin is $τ$. If the force acts on a particle whose position vector is $2\overset{^}{i} + 2\overset{^}{j} + \overset{^}{k}$, then the value of $τ$ will be

questions.solution:
Using the determinant rule to find the torque

& $\overset{→}{τ} = \overset{→}{r} \times \overset{→}{F} = \left|$\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 2 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & 3 & - 7\end{cases}$\right|$

$= \overset{^}{i} \left(-14 - 3\right) - \overset{^}{j} \left(-$14 - 5\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(6 - 10\right)$

Thus, the value of~$\overset{→}{τ} = - 17\overset{^}{i} + 19\overset{^}{j} - 4\overset{^}{k}$

$

questions.q: If a solid sphere of mass $5$ kg and a disc of mass $4$ kg have the same radius, then the ratio of moment of inertia of the disc about a tangent in its plane to the moment of inertia of the sphere about its tangent will be~$\dfrac{x}{7}$.~The value of $x$ is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Moment of inertia of the& solid sphere about any diameter is given by,& $\dfrac{2{m}_{1}R^{2}}{5}$.

Using parallel axis theorem, we get

${I}_{solid sphere } = \dfrac{2}{5}{m}_{1}R^{2} + {m}_{1}R^{2} = \dfrac{7}{5}{m}_{1}R^{2}$

$= \dfrac{7}{5} \times 5R^{2}$

$= 7R^{2}$

Moment of inertia of the disc about the diameter is given by,~$\dfrac{{m}_{2}R^{2}}{4}$.

Now using parallel axis theorem, we get

${I}_{disc } = \dfrac{{m}_{2}R^{2}}{4} + {m}_{2}R^{2} = \dfrac{5}{4}{m}_{2}R^{2}$

$= \dfrac{5}{4} \times 4R^{2}$

$= 5R^{2}$

Therefore,$\dfrac{I\text{disc}}{I\text{soild sphere}} = \dfrac{5}{7}$

Thus,~$x = 5$.

questions.q: A metre scale is balanced on a knife edge at its centre. questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let the mass of the scale be& $m$.

The centre of mass of the scale will be at~$50$ cm.

Applying torque balance,~

$0 = mg \times \left(50 - 40\right) - 2 \times 10g \times \left(40 - 10\right) ⇒ m = 60g = 6 \times {10}^{- 2}kg$

questions.q:
A particle of mass $m$~is moving in time $t$~on a trajectory given by,~

$\overset{→}{r} = 10\alphat^{2}\overset{^}{i} + 5\beta\left(t - 5\right)\overset{^}{j}$

where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are dimensional constants.

The angular momentum of the particle becomes the same as it was for $t = 0$ at time~t =_____ seconds.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\overset{→}{r} = 10\alphat^{2}\overset{^}{i} + 5\beta\left(t - 5\right)\overset{^}{j}$

$\overset{→}{v} = 20\alpha + \overset{^}{i} + 5\beta\overset{^}{j}$

$\overset{→}{L} = m \left(\overset{→}{r} \times \overset{→}{v}\right)

$= m \left[$10\alphat^{2}\overset{^}{i} + 5$\beta \left($t - 5\right)\overset{^}{j}\right]$\times \lleft[20\alpha\overset{^}{i} ++5\beta\overset{^}{j}]

$\overset{→}{L} = m \left[50\alpha\betat^{2}\overset{^}{k} -100\alpha\beta\left(t^{2} - 5t\right)\overset{^}{k}\right]$

At $t = 0, \overset{→}{L} = \overset{→}{0}$

$50\alpha\betat^{2} -100\alpha\beta\left(t^{2} - 5t\right) = 0$

$t - 2\left(t - 5\right) = 0$

$t = 10sec$

questions.q: A ring and a solid sphere roll down the same inclined plane without slipping. They start from rest. The radii of both bodies are identical and the ratio of their kinetic energies is $\dfrac{7}{x}$, where $x$ is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In pure rolling work done by friction is zero. Hence, potential energy is converted into kinetic energy. Since initially the ring and the sphere have same potential energy, finally they will have same kinetic energy too.
$∴$ Ratio of kinetic energies $= 1$
$⇒ \dfrac{7}{x} = 1 ⇒ x = 7$
